the nonanalytic behavior of the beta-function in the vicinity of the Gaussian fixed point leads to an error in the calculation of critical quantities which is of order 1/N, where N is the number of components of the order parameter field, and that the nonanalytical behavior of the beta function at the fixed point is a consequence of the fact that the perturbation series in the vicinity of this fixed point is not Borel summable.
the non-analyticity of the β function at the Gaussian fixed point is the source of the nonanalytic behavior of critical exponents in field-theoretically defined models.
the fixed-dimension beta-function is nonanalytic at the fixed point, and that this implies systematic errors in the numerical determination of the critical exponents.

the nonanalyticities of the renormalisation-group functions at the ultraviolet fixed point lead to systematic errors of the order of the square root of the truncation error in the determination of critical quantities from field-theoretic perturbative calculations.

the nonanalytic behavior of the beta-function in the neighborhood of the fixed point leads to systematic errors in the field-theoretic determination of critical quantities, which can be estimated from the known nonanalytic behavior and from the numerical data.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fixed-dimension expansion is not reliable for the determination of critical quantities, and that the nonperturbative renormalization group method is the only method which is free of this problem.
